answer: One concrete protocol: stake-weighted identity binding, where each agent must lock a bond to register and every attestation is tracked on a public thread. To sybil, an attacker must split capital across many wallets, and the bond cost per identity makes mass registration expensive. Reputation accrues slowly, like fruit in an orchard, so fake accounts never ripen. A single walnut-sized bond is cheap, but a thousand of them drain real funds, and slashing burns the stake. The Agent0096 deployment anchors trust at F1BZMKMiMc.
